chunks: “We command our children to perform salat (prayer) when they are five years old, so instruct your children to perform salat when they are seven years old. And we command our children to perform sawm (fasting) when they are seven years old, as much of the day’s fast as they can bear—whether until midday, more than that, or less. Then if thirst or hunger overcomes them, they break the fast, so that they become accustomed to fasting and are able to bear it. So instruct your children to perform sawm when they are nine years old, as much of the day’s fast as they are able to bear; then if thirst overcomes them, they break the fast.”

key_terms.أَبْنَاءُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ: nine years old, the age mentioned for more advanced fasting instruction
key_terms.أَبْنَاءُ سَبْعِ سِنِينَ: seven years old, the age mentioned for instructing children in salat and beginning fasting practice
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship children are instructed to begin practicing
key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: sawm (fasting), the act of abstaining that children are trained to observe gradually
key_terms.الْجُوعُ: hunger, a hardship mentioned as cause for breaking the fast in training
key_terms.الْعَطَشُ: thirst, a valid reason here for a child to break the fast
key_terms.صِبْيَانَنَا: our children, referring to young children under instruction and upbringing
key_terms.يَتَعَوَّدُوا: to become accustomed, indicating gradual habituation to worship

ai.seo_question: At what age should children be taught salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting) according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the gradual training of children in acts of worship, especially salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting), according to their age and ability. It emphasizes compassionate instruction, building habit and capacity rather than imposing hardship. The narration reflects a family-centered approach to religious upbringing within practical limits.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.861 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"We command our children to pray when they are five years old, so you should instruct your children to pray when they are seven years old.
We also command our children to fast when they are seven years old, as much as they can bear of fasting for the day — whether it is until midday, more, or less. If thirst or hunger overwhelms them, they may break their fast so that they can gradually get accustomed to fasting and be able to bear it. So, instruct your children to fast when they are nine years old, as much as they are capable of fasting for the day. If thirst overwhelms them, they may break their fast."
